revision_note: accepted_look: block-floor friction 0.58 -> 0.20 (sealed oak floor), block start 0.58 m further from the sponge (x -0.72 -> -1.30 m), initial speed 3.2 -> 2.8 m/s (fast_block 4.8 -> 4.2 m/s, still x1.5), preset added block on the exact midpoint (x -0.35 -> -0.635 m); sponge, leg, masses, solver settings unchanged; motion lasts about 2.5x longer

reference_basis.product_geometry: A recognizable 160 mm yellow open-cell household sponge with a green fibrous scouring layer starts 8 mm clear of the left face of a full-height wooden table leg. There is no hidden plate, pedestal, adhesive strip, or rear restraint.
reference_basis.material: Effective 0.32 MPa, 48 kg/m3 open-cell polyurethane-like foam, nu=0.30, represented by Stable Neo-Hookean tetrahedral FEM. This is a benchmark-scale effective model selected for observable flexible-foam response, not a proprietary foam calibration or a full crushable-foam law.
reference_basis.mounting: The sponge has zero constrained FEM vertices and rests freely on the floor. The wood block first strikes the sponge; the translated sponge then closes an 8 mm gap and contacts the fixed table leg. The 105 x 120 x 790 mm proxy represents the contacted leg of a fixed 28 kg table assembly and touches the floor.
reference_basis.heavy_edit: The benchmark edit changes only the rigid-body mass parameter from 2 kg to 20 kg. Geometry and visible material remain unchanged.
reference_basis.floor_contact: The rendered lacquered oak plank floor is the fixed z=0 collision plane. Block-floor kinetic friction mu=0.20 (smooth finished wood on a sealed wood floor; textbook wood-on-wood kinetic value); sponge-floor friction mu=0.64. Both contacts are solved inside the same frictional IPC scene.

asset_basis.floor: Poly Haven Wood Floor (wood_floor) 4K CC0 oak planks, 1.7 m metric UV, planks along the direction of travel, thin lacquer coat; bump only, the contact plane stays at z=0.
asset_basis.wall: Poly Haven White Plaster 02 4K CC0 scan under an opaque off-white paint coat, 1 m metric UV, with broad trowel undulation.
asset_basis.table: Poly Haven Wooden Table 02 CC0, 4K glTF; its front-left leg face is registered on the 105 x 120 x 790 mm fixed collision cuboid (x=0.118 m).
asset_basis.block: Exact collision box with a 3 mm render-only edge radius; Poly Haven dark_wood 2K CC0 (toned down) with the grain along the block, procedural growth rings on the saw-cut ends, worn arrises and dings.
asset_basis.sponge: Native FEM surface with a yellow open-cell foam body and a green non-woven scouring layer; procedural pores and fibres follow the deforming FEM surface.
asset_basis.room: Back wall 1.05 m behind the path with skirting; props from Poly Haven (CC0): wooden_display_shelves_01, wooden_stool_02, wicker_basket_02, fancy_picture_frame_01 (leaning, back outwards), potted_plant_01; daylight from a window in the left wall (sun + kloofendal_48d_partly_cloudy_puresky sky).

model_scope: A fixed full-table assembly represented at contact by a solid table-leg proxy, a sealed oak plank floor, one or two affine rigid wooden blocks, and a completely unrestrained open-cell sponge coupled in one frictional IPC scene. The sequence is block-to-sponge followed by moving sponge-to-leg contact. The foam law is selected for clearly observable elastic compression and recovery, not for product-specific force-displacement prediction.
